rationale: The same material imposes different effective demands depending on relevant schemas.
Examples are most useful for novices and can become redundant as expertise grows.
Generation before instruction requires enough knowledge to produce interpretable attempts.
Responsibility should move from external support toward learner monitoring and control.
Worked examples can reduce unproductive novice search on structured tasks.
Coherence and integrated references reduce avoidable processing and split attention.
As knowledge grows, learners need to retrieve and generate rather than continue copying full solutions.
Explanation can focus attention on solution decisions, but prompts must be accurate and proportionate.
Spaced retrieval combines the retention advantages of distributed encounters and active recall.
Corrective feedback repairs failed or erroneous retrieval.
Interleaving often spaces each category, though its distinctive target is discrimination and strategy selection.
Mixed practice can support selection under varied conditions when categories are appropriate for comparison.
Explaining deep relations can help abstract structure beyond surface features.
External performance information can correct monitoring and guide strategy changes.
Formative inferences require construct-aligned elicitation and interpretation.
Feedback is one possible evidence-contingent next action inside the cycle.
A validity argument depends on explicit cognition, observation, and interpretation links.
Construct-irrelevant access barriers undermine intended score interpretations.
Accessible delivery and interaction are prerequisites for fair digital assessment.
Claims about retention or generalization require observations beyond immediate practiced performance.
Content-appropriate complementary media do not validate matching instruction to a preferred modality label.
Mapping the same relation across forms can prepare use beyond one representation.
Substantive co-construction may instantiate interactive engagement; mere group seating does not.
Productive failure is a narrower, specified generation-then-consolidation sequence within the broader struggle label.
Observed difficulty is not evidence that a high-fidelity productive-failure design is present.
Agency, competence, and belonging can support sustained self-regulation when effective strategies are available.
A brief malleability message is not equivalent to providing autonomy, competence support, belonging, effective strategies, or resources.
Target, language, pacing, and support should follow observed development and context rather than a fixed age script.
Responsive adult guidance can scaffold a clear goal while preserving child agency.
Meaningful bounded choice and identity-safe relationships can support autonomy and belonging.
Proactive options may reduce barriers but do not replace WCAG conformance, accommodations, or assistive technology.
Accurate decoding supports text access while oral language and comprehension knowledge must develop in parallel.
Academic language and vocabulary support disciplinary text understanding without replacing content.
Teacher modeling and mentor texts externalize decisions before support fades toward independent writing.
Writers need usable information and revision opportunities to refine decisions.
A progression should be navigated from observed mathematical strategies, not chronological age alone.
Effective intervention explicitly connects selected models, language, quantities, and symbols.
Comparing alternative methods practices discrimination and procedural choice after initial acquisition.
Crosscutting concepts and repeated practices are intended to connect ideas across phenomena and disciplines.
Testing and debugging turn artifact behavior into information for revision.
Self-direction depends on monitoring, strategy selection, and feedback rather than adult age.
Workplace learning succeeds only when knowledge generalizes and is maintained in the work environment.
Focused correction depends on valid, specific performance information.
Focused repetitions need scheduling and recovery; massed hours are not the target construct.
